recent_articles.title: TANUVAS invites applications for UG courses - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Tanuvas)** has opened its application portal for undergraduate courses, including Bachelor's in Veterinary Sciences and Animal Husbandry, and various B. Tech programs. Applications are open from 10 a.m. on May 25 to 5 p.m. on June 17 through the university's website: https://adm.tanuvas.ac.in.  Candidates can find details regarding seat reservations for NRIs, NRI-sponsored candidates, and foreign nationals on the portal.

recent_articles.title: Innovation begins with understanding the fundamentals: Prakash Balasubramanian - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prakash Balasubramanian**, senior director at **Infineon Technologies**, emphasized the importance of foundational knowledge for technological breakthroughs during the inauguration of "Nirmaan Utsav" in Kalaburagi city. He highlighted the evolution of technologies over decades and urged students to think innovatively. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Shaloo encouraged students to combine academic learning with practical experience and stay updated on emerging fields like drones, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity. HKE Society president and MLC Shashil Namoshi noted that **PDA Engineering College** is nurturing future-ready students through events like "Nirmaan Utsav."

recent_articles.title: Conference on higher education held - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jebi Mather**, MP, emphasized the need for continuous modernization of Kerala's higher education sector during a conference on 'Higher Education Reforms'.  **Prof. Junaid Bushiri**, Vice-Chancellor of Cochin University of Science and Technology, highlighted the importance of developing employability skills alongside academic achievements. The conference, organized by **Kerala Principals’ Council**, featured sessions led by prominent figures in academia and literature.

recent_articles.title: Four from Telangana State colleges to go on Sakura Science Programme - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Four students** from Telangana have been selected to participate in the **Japan Science and Technology Agency’s (JST)** SAKURA Science Programme. The seven-day program, starting May 24th, will allow the students to visit advanced scientific institutions, interact with scientists, and gain exposure to Japan's innovation in education and science. The students were selected through district-level nominations and a state-level screening test conducted earlier this year.

recent_articles.title: Turkiye shutters liberal Istanbul university seized in criminal probe | Education News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Recep Tayyip Erdogan** revoked the operating license for Istanbul Bilgi University, a private university known for its liberal values, citing insufficient education standards. The closure, effective immediately, follows a criminal investigation into the institution's parent company and has sparked protests from students who will now continue their studies at Mimar Sinan University. **The Council of Higher Education** promised to ensure student safety during this transition.

recent_articles.title: Over 2.3 lakh students register for TNEA 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Over 2.34 lakh candidates have registered for the **Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions (TNEA) 2026** portal, with many completing application and fee payment processes. The registration deadline is June 2nd, followed by certificate uploads until June 6th.  Random number assignments will occur on June 5th, with certificate verification starting June 8th and a rank list published on June 29th. Counselling for special category students, including those in the eminent sportspersons category, is expected to begin in July after Class XII results are released.

recent_articles.title: Minority commission recommends upgrading Pallikkal govt. school in Wayanad - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Kerala State Commission for Minorities** recommended that the **Pallikkal Government Lower Primary (LP) School** in Wayanad be upgraded to an upper primary (UP) school during the 2026-27 academic year. The recommendation was made following a petition submitted by the school's management and favorable response from the Wayanad Deputy Director of Education, who acknowledged the school's facilities and student population.  The school has all necessary infrastructure for an UP section, including smart classrooms and additional construction under the Wayanad Package.

recent_articles.title: NCERT book row: SC modifies earlier order concerning 3 academics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** on Friday reversed its March 11 order that directed the Centre, States, and others to disassociate from three academics involved in a controversial chapter of the NCERT's Class 8 social science textbook. The court left it up to the Centre, states, universities, and institutions to make their own decisions regarding the issue without being influenced by its previous observations.  The Court also clarified that its comments were made in context of the content and not the individuals involved.

recent_articles.title: VIT-A.P. University celebrates ninth anniversary at Amaravati campus - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **HCLTech** Head of Campus Relations Director Prasath P. emphasized the importance of industry-academia collaboration during his speech at the 9th University Day celebrations at **VIT-A.P. University**. He commended the university's efforts in research, entrepreneurship, and community service, stating that graduates from such institutions are well-prepared for the global workforce.

recent_articles.title: States should be allowed to conduct CET for medical courses: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** called for the decentralization of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and urged **States** to have the opportunity to conduct their own Common Entrance Tests (CET) for medical courses. He argued that education is a concurrent list subject, allowing states to independently administer entrance exams for professional courses within the federal system.

recent_articles.title: Lakshmi could have been a child bride - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lakshmi**, a 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh, wrote a song expressing her desire to continue her education and resist early marriage. Her father initially dismissed the message but was persuaded by **anganwadi workers** and **village pradhan**.  The village now features painted messages advocating for change in response to Lakshmi's powerful lyrics.

recent_articles.title: IT-based skill training launched for inmates at Visakhapatnam Central Jail - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andhra Pradesh** Prisons Department and the **Skill Development Institute (SDI)**, Visakhapatnam, launched an IT-based skill development course for inmates at the Visakhapatnam Central Jail. The "Office Assistant" program, inaugurated by **Visakhapatnam District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore**, aims to equip inmates with industry-oriented skills and improve their employability prospects after release.  The two-month course covers computer applications, office administration, digital communication, and employability skills, with successful participants receiving a certification from SDI Visakhapatnam.

recent_articles.title: Charges dismissed against official at school where 6-year-old shot teacher
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ebony Parker**, former assistant principal at a Virginia elementary school, has been cleared of all charges against her stemming from the shooting incident in January 2023. **Judge Rebecca Robinson** dismissed eight felony counts, including disregard for life, after the defense argued that the state had not presented sufficient evidence to prove their case. The six-year-old student who fired a single shot at teacher **Abigail Zwerner**, who suffered injuries requiring surgery, is being cared for by his mother, **Deja Taylor**.

recent_articles.title: Russia’s Sechenov University assigns ‘Visiting Professor’ status to Basappa Salundi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sechenov First Moscow State Medical (SMSM) University** in Russia has appointed **Basappa Salundi**, chairman of the Department of Organic Chemistry at the **University of Mysore**, as a 'Visiting Professor'. This honorary title, established in 2025, does not involve formal employment or salary and is awarded to recognized external specialists. The university hopes this will enhance its prestige and competitiveness by attracting leading scientists who can facilitate increased publications and international grants.

recent_articles.title: After State-run schools, Vande Mataram now compulsory in all Bengal madrasas - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education** has mandated the singing of "Vande Mataram" during assembly prayers in all government, aided, and recognized madrasas across the state. The order, issued by the Director of Madrasa Education, states that this is effective immediately and supersedes previous practices.  This decision follows a similar mandate for state-run schools announced earlier in May.

recent_articles.title: I tried to buy a Cambridge paper online, this is what happened - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: This summer, leaked Cambridge International Examinations (CAIE) papers have caused widespread disruption for Pakistani students.  **Cambridge Assessment International Education (CAIE**) reported the theft and unauthorized sharing of examination papers on May 7th and 14th, with evidence being sent to platforms where the leaks circulated. The agency is investigating both incidents thoroughly through digital forensics, analysis of online platforms, and cooperation with law enforcement. **Anant Nanda**, an A Level student from Lahore, discovered a Discord server called "Cambridge Leaks" that sells leaked papers for $100 each.  He attempted to purchase a Mathematics Paper 1 exam paper, which was available on the website for sale. The CAIE has assured students and schools that it is working to protect them from this problem. Parents are concerned about fair assessments and the future of their children's education.

recent_articles.title: Doctor can’t enrol as advocate without cancelling registration: HC - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Kerala High Court** ruled that a registered medical practitioner cannot be enrolled as an advocate, unless she cancels her homeopathic license. The court cited the **Bar Council of Kerala (BCK)**'s duty to ensure applicants are not engaged in other professions and the **Kerala State Medical Practitioners Act, 2021**, which prohibits practicing medicine alongside another profession.  The court upheld the BCK's decision to deny the petitioner's enrollment application.

recent_articles.title: TGBCESDTC to conduct 4-day AI and life skills training programme - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Telangana BC Employability Skill Development and Training Centre (TGBCESDTC)**, in collaboration with the **Magic Bus India Foundation**, will host a four-day interactive workshop from May 21 to June 11 across various districts of Telangana. The program aims to introduce district-level youth to artificial intelligence technologies and enhance their employability skills.  Interested youth are advised to contact their nearest TGBCESDTC centers for enrollment and further information.

recent_articles.title: NCC annual training camp begins - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The NCC Group Training Centre, West Hill**, hosted the annual training camp for 380 cadets from **Kozhikode, Kannur, and Palakkad districts**.  The ten-day program, led by **Col. Venkatesan R., Commanding Officer of the NCC 9 Kerala Girls Battalion**, aims to foster civic sense and social responsibility in participants through classes on personality development, health and hygiene, self-defense, and NCC subject training. The camp concludes on May 22nd.

recent_articles.title: Medical Education Minister demands court-monitored probe into NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil** criticized the ongoing investigation into the NEET question paper leak, calling for a court-monitored probe. He expressed concerns that the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**'s current investigation lacked transparency and confidence, suggesting powerful individuals were involved in orchestrating the scandal to manipulate MBBS seat sales.

recent_articles.title: Students get clarity on career choices at The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling Fair in Mysuru - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Students** attending the **Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling Fair-2026** at **Vidya Vardhaka College of Engineering** in Mysuru sought guidance on their future career paths.  Experts from various fields provided information and advice to over 500 students, many accompanied by their parents, helping them navigate available career options based on individual interests and aptitudes.

recent_articles.title: Why Robert F. Smith’s Morehouse surprise donation mattered even more after graduation day
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Robert F. Smith**, an entrepreneur, made a significant donation of $34 million to **Morehouse College** in 2019, covering the student debt for the graduating class and that of their parents. The gesture resonated widely due to its impact on both students' immediate financial burdens and the broader issue of educational debt in African-American communities.  This event highlighted the significant role family debt plays in college expenses and sparked a conversation about educational equality and financial empowerment within historically black colleges and universities (HBCUs).

recent_articles.title: Results show it is possible to raise quality without failing students: Sivankutty - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V. Sivankutty**, former Minister for General Education, congratulated students on the high pass percentage of 99.07 in the State syllabus Class X exams. He acknowledged the hard work and dedication of students and their families, emphasizing that this was not the end but a new beginning. **Sivankutty** also highlighted the changes in question paper pattern aimed at preparing students for national-level entrance tests, stating that these adjustments did not negatively impact student performance.

recent_articles.title: Tennessee school district bans Alex Haley’s Roots under 2022 state law | Tennessee | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Knox County Schools (KCS)** in Tennessee have removed the novel "Roots" from school library shelves due to a state law requiring review of materials for appropriateness. The decision, made under the Age-Appropriate Materials Act, follows a review by KCS's book-banning committee which deemed an excerpt not age-appropriate.  The author's grandson and advocates for free expression criticize the ban as short-sighted and harmful to students' understanding of history.

recent_articles.title: The $55 million blueprint: How New York’s busiest library swapped worn-out shelves for a civic living room
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **New York Public Library** received a $55 million donation from the **Stavros Niarchos Foundation** to renovate its Mid-Manhattan branch, which had become outdated due to high usage. The renovation transformed the library into a modern hub for learning, interaction, and professional development with features like open spaces, learning zones, and an outdoor terrace.  The redesigned space saw significant increases in visits and circulation numbers, demonstrating the potential of public libraries as democratic resources for everyday citizens.

recent_articles.title: Three-day Mohiniyattam masterclass at Fort Kochi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Kalamandalam**, a performance arts institution, is hosting a three-day masterclass on Mohiniyattam from May 22 to 24. The event, part of the **Kalamandalam's Masterclass series**, will be led by artiste **Methil Devika**.  Participants must have at least five years of experience in an Indian classical dance form and apply online before May 19th. For more information visit www.kalamandalam.ac.in or call 98471 88288.

recent_articles.title: US justice department accuses Yale medical school of illegally using race in admissions | Yale University | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **US Department of Justice** accused **Yale University** of illegally considering race in admissions to its medical school, alleging that Black and Hispanic students have a significantly higher chance of admission than white or Asian students despite lower academic credentials. Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights **Harmeet Dhillon** stated that the department is seeking a voluntary resolution agreement with the university but has the authority to take legal action if necessary. This follows a similar accusation against the **University of California, Los Angeles**, and aligns with the Trump administration's efforts to restrict race-based admissions policies.

recent_articles.title: Govt orders inquiry into Cambridge exam leaks - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The interior ministry** directed the **National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA)** to investigate the alleged leak of Cambridge International Education (CIE) exam papers, in coordination with CIE. The investigation was prompted by a meeting chaired by Interior Secretary Muhammad Khurram Agha, where concerns were raised about the second suspected leak of an O Level Mathematics paper and the potential theft of exam materials. **The British deputy high commissioner** stated that the matter appeared to involve theft rather than a true leak, while **CIE representatives** assured the forum that they maintain strict standards for examination integrity. The meeting also saw discussions on strengthening CIE's system capacity to address weaknesses in the examination process and ensuring transparency.

recent_articles.title: SRMIST, The Hindu to organise webinar on c - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST)**, in partnership with **The Hindu**, is hosting a webinar titled "Career Beyond the Obvious: Unlocking New Pathways in Humanities and Sciences." The event will feature experts from various fields discussing how skills in humanities and sciences are opening doors to careers in research, technology, media, analytics, and more. Panelists include A. Vinay Kumar, Dean of Faculty of Sciences and Humanities at **SRMIST**, Deepa Sethi, Executive Chair of Globe, IIM Kozhikode, and Kamal Karanth, Co-founder of Xpheno Private Limited.  The webinar is part of the Future Career Conversations series and will be hosted by Prince Frederick of **The Hindu**.

recent_articles.title: NEET-UG, 2026 paper leak: Experts call for reforms in exam process, exemption of State-government seats - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Doctors’ Association for Social Equality (DASE)** general secretary G.R. Ravindranath and **Indian Medical Association (IMA)** former president Rajeev Jayadevan have called for compulsory registration of all medical entrance exam coaching centers, a computerised NEET exam, and exemption of state-government controlled medical seats from the single-window national system to prevent malpractices in the exam.  They also suggested free coaching centers with boarding facilities for poor students and the use of technology like encrypted questions and multi-session testing to ensure a fair and merit-based process.

recent_articles.title: ‘Limited’ religious symbols to be allowed with uniforms in Karnataka schools and colleges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka government** withdrew its 2022 order requiring prescribed uniforms in educational institutions and replaced it with a new order allowing students to wear “limited” traditional and faith-based symbols alongside their uniforms.  Minister for School Education and Literacy **Madhu Bangarappa** stated that the decision aims to promote secular values and equal respect for all religions and traditions within schools, while maintaining institutional discipline.

recent_articles.title: NSUI holds protest outside Education Minister’s residence over NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Members of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI)** protested outside **Dharmendra Pradhan's** residence in Delhi, demanding his resignation following allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The protesters accused the Education Minister of failing to protect students and demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the incident, along with action against those involved. **The National Testing Agency (NTA)** cancelled the exam and announced it would be retaken at a later date.

recent_articles.title: The south London community where ‘pioneering’ scholarship choristers are made | London | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **St John the Divine**, **Kennington (SJDK)**, a church in south London, has produced several young choristers who have secured scholarships to prestigious music institutions.  The church's youth choral program, which began in 2013, aims to remove barriers that keep working-class children from classical music. The program provides transportation and snacks for rehearsals, making it accessible for families with limited resources. **Ed Picton-Turbervill**, an award-winning composer and organist, credits the program's success in fostering musical talent and breaking down racial prejudice within the community.  **N’raeah**, a four-year-old chorister from south London, has been accepted into St Paul's Cathedral school, a testament to the impact of the program.

recent_articles.title: Good show by Ernakulam schools in Class 12 exams - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Schools** under the **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** in Ernakulam district achieved high pass rates in Class 12 examinations.  **Bhavan’s Vidya Mandir, Elamakkara**, and **Rajagiri Public School, Kalamassery** led with the highest number of distinctions, exceeding 100 students each. Several schools recorded 100% pass rates, including **Sacred Heart CMI Public School, Thevara** and **Mar Thoma Public School, Thengode**.

recent_articles.title: Cambridge confirms leak of AS-level Mathematics paper, postpones upcoming exam as 'precautionary step' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Cambridge International Education (CIE)** confirmed the leak of an AS-level Mathematics exam paper on May 12th and postponed another exam scheduled for Friday, May 15th.  The board is investigating the incident and working to understand the extent of the leak. **Uzma Yousuf**, Country Director of Pakistan, stated that the board's decisions were made by experienced professionals who prioritize fairness and reliability in grading. She emphasized that leaks are rare and stressed the importance of trusting official statements from CIE. The release date for AS- and A-Level results remains unchanged (August 11th).

recent_articles.title: Cancellation sparks anger, anxiety among aspirants in Telangana - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **NEET (UG)** 2026 has been canceled following allegations of a paper leak, causing widespread frustration and anxiety among students, parents, and educators in **Telangana**.  Long-term aspirants like Mounika U. expressed disappointment over the system failure, while **G. Vijay Kumar**, a NEET trainer, highlighted the emotional impact on young students. The **Students’ Federation of India (Telangana)** criticized the government's handling of the situation, calling it an "administrative failure." Protests are planned by student groups and organizations demanding fair and transparent examination processes.

recent_articles.title: The $1.8 billion pivot: How Michael Bloomberg’s historic gift rewrote the rules of college access | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Michael Bloomberg** donated $1.8 billion to **Johns Hopkins University**, the largest donation in American history, to fund undergraduate scholarships and eliminate financial barriers for prospective students. This move aims to address a psychological obstacle preventing talented individuals from low-income backgrounds from pursuing higher education due to high tuition fees. The endowment will ensure that all accepted students can attend without incurring debt, fostering an environment where merit is prioritized over wealth.  This historic gift signifies a shift in the focus of philanthropy towards creating opportunities for excellence and dismantling financial barriers in higher education.

recent_articles.title: School education index: Kerala betters grade, score - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite the denial of funds by the **Union government**, **Kerala** has improved its performance in the **Union Ministry of Education’s Performance Grading Index 2.0 for States/Union Territories (UT) for the year 2024-25**. The state received a Prachesta-2 grade, an improvement from Prachesta-3 in 2023-24, with scores rising from 594.2 to 687.7.  **Kerala** achieved the topmost Utkarsh grade (72.8-80) in access and the Uttam-1 grade (81-90.9) in teacher education and training, among other achievements. The report highlights Kerala's progress despite challenges, including a lack of funding from the **Union government**.

recent_articles.title: What you need to know about Karnataka’s Rohith Vemula Bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Karnataka** government has approved the revised **Rohith Vemula** Bill, 2026. The bill aims to prevent discrimination and injustice for students, faculty, and staff from scheduled castes and tribes (SC/ST) by guaranteeing equal access to education in all higher educational institutions across the state.

recent_articles.title: NEET-UG examination 2026: One suspect arrested from Nashik - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Testing Agency (NTA)** cancelled the NEET-UG examination for 2026 after an alleged paper leak, leading to the arrest of a suspect in **Maharashtra**. The Rajasthan Police requested the **Maharashtra police** to detain the individual who was apprehended after changing his appearance.  The cancellation has drawn criticism from opposition leaders, including **Rohit Pawar**, who pointed out that the state government's new law against paper leaks is insufficient and called for stricter action against those involved. A CBI inquiry into the matter has been initiated.

recent_articles.title: PMDC says medical students must qualify for MDCAT, obtain registration before going abroad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC)** announced new regulations for students pursuing medical or dental education abroad. The PMDC stated that all students must qualify for the **MDCAT** examination, obtain registration with the council, and verify the foreign institution's accreditation by either the **World Federation for Medical Education (WFME)** or the **World Directory of Medical Schools**.  The PMDC emphasized the importance of ensuring a minimum of 6,200 hours of education, at least 80% attendance over five years, language proficiency in English or local languages, and passing the **National Registration Examination** for registration in Pakistan upon completion. The PMDC also directed students to provide complete details of their residence and contact information before departure, as well as secure a multiple-entry visa valid for the duration of their studies.

recent_articles.title: Cambridge AS-level Mathematics paper allegedly leaked, students claim - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Cambridge International Education (CIE)**, part of **Cambridge University Press and Assessment**, is facing accusations of paper leaks for the AS-level Mathematics exam in Karachi. Students allege that the Tuesday's exam was identical to a solved paper they saw on social media.  **CIE** states that it investigates all allegations of paper leaks but does not comment on individual reports. The organization has offered resits for candidates impacted by previous leaks and is currently investigating this latest allegation.

recent_articles.title: Mexico cancels plans to end school year early for World Cup
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mexico's** government has reversed its decision to end the school year early due to concerns raised by parents and education experts. The original plan, announced in May, aimed to ease traffic during the **Fifa World Cup** and a heatwave.  After backlash from the National Union of Parents, President **Claudia Sheinbaum** clarified that ending classes early was only a proposal. The decision has been scrapped, with classes now scheduled to finish on July 15th.

recent_articles.title: NEET-UG 2026 cancelled LIVE: CBI to probe paper leak allegations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Testing Agency (NTA)** cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 exam held on May 3rd after allegations of a paper leak. The decision follows investigations by both the **Rajasthan Special Operations Group** and the **CBI**, with the government approving the cancellation to ensure transparency.  The examination will be re-conducted at a later date, details of which will be announced separately.

recent_articles.title: NSUI protests after NTA cancels NEET-UG 2026 over paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A massive protest organized by the **National Students' Union of India (NSUI)** erupted outside the **Shastri Bhawan** on Tuesday, May 12, 2026, demanding justice for students alleging a paper leak in the NEET-UG exam.  The protest saw members of the **Congress party's student wing** participate, holding signs and slogans criticizing the government's handling of the situation. The **National Testing Agency (NTA)** canceled the examination following investigations by the **Rajasthan Special Operations Group (SOG) and the CBI**.  The NSUI accused the central government of failing to protect students and demanded the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and a ban on the **NTA**.
